qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Advanced MEMS and vertical probe cards feature proprietary micro-fabrication IP and tight engineering integration with leading chip designers. However, probe cards are custom-engineered per chip tape-out and subject to constant dual-sourcing bake-offs against FormFactor and Asian competitors. Concentrated customers (foundries, integrated device manufacturers) exert strong pricing leverage, compressing operating margins by ~17-18 percentage points between 2022 and 2025.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (pricing power/proof of moat, REJECT). World-class MEMS probe card manufacturer faces intense head-to-head dual-sourcing re-bidding against FormFactor and Asian competitors for each chip tape-out. Concentrated semiconductor buyers exercise strong purchasing power, causing EBIT margins to compress by ~17-18 percentage points (from 37.8% in 2022 to 20.5% in 2025) and preventing peak-to-peak EPS compounding.
qualitative.evidence: Technoprobe's revenues grew from €548.9M in FY22 to €628.4M in FY25, yet EBIT fell 38% from €207.4M to €129.0M, and Net Income plunged from €147.9M to €97.7M (Owner EPS dropped from €0.25 to €0.15). Operating margins experienced severe structural dilution (from 37.8% down to 20.5%) driven by mix shifts, DIS integration, and customer pricing pressure across competitive node transitions, failing the Munger standard for cycle-neutral pricing power.
